name: Rolling Half-Kelly Ledger Sizing
note: The signal is a deliberately fixed harness - a 20-bar Donchian breakout, out on a 10-bar low, stop at 2 ATR - so the only thing under test is the QUANTITY rule. A rolling ledger of the last N closed trades on this symbol gives W, the average win and the average loss, hence f* = W - (1-W)/R; the share count is kelly_c * f* of equity divided by the per-share stop distance, capped at risk_cap, and a NEGATIVE f* vetoes the trade outright. ONE GAP HAD TO BE FILLED: as literally written the veto is absorbing, because f* is only recomputed when a trade closes and no trade can close once trading stops - measured on the probe it froze every symbol at exactly 30 trades and left the whole grid inert. probe_n therefore takes one floor-sized trade after that many consecutive vetoes so the ledger can refresh; the sweep includes an arm large enough to reproduce the literal absorbing rule.
source: Edward O. Thorp, 'The Kelly Criterion in Blackjack, Sports Betting, and the Stock Market' (2006/2007), open PDF at https://gwern.net/doc/statistics/decision/2006-thorp.pdf - the half-Kelly growth/drawdown result is in the fractional-Kelly section.
